results.title: Germany's Organic Farming Expansion: Challenges and Strategies
results.content: 🧭 How to apply it (practical steps) 1) Transition a portion of conventional farmland to organic practices 2) Implement integrated pest management techniques to reduce reliance on pesticides 3) Collaborate with local conservation groups to promote biodiversity on farmland 4) Conduct regular soil testing to monitor health and fertility 5) Explore government grants for sustainable farming initiatives, if available 📏 Metrics to watch • Crop yield per hectare • Pesticide residue levels in soil and produce • Biodiversity index on farmland • Percentage of organic vs. conventional farming practices ✅ Key takeaways • Embrace organic farming practices to promote sustainability • Prioritize integrated pest management techniques over pesticide usage • Collaborate with stakeholders to enhance biodiversity on farmland • Monitor and adjust agricultural practices based on environmental metrics What steps can we take to strike a balance between increasing productivity and preserving the environment in agriculture?

results.title: empirical results of a survey in 218 farms - AGRIS
results.content: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. # New insights into organic farming in Germany – empirical results of a survey in 218 farms. A comprehensive description of the recent structure, performance and developments of organic farming in Germany does not exist. Because of this gap the Institute of Organic Farming and the Institute of Farm Economics of the German Federal Agricultural Research Centre (FAL) have carried out an interdisciplinary empirical analysis of the state of the art of Organic Farming in Germany in 2002-2003. important function of the study was to establish a long lasting research-organic farming network. Farm economists, organic crop production specialists, organic livestock specialists and sociologists are member of the scientific network. 218 randomly chosen farms throughout. Germany have been surveyed in 2002/2003. variables per farm have been gathered. This bibliographic record has been provided by. International Centre for Research in Organic Food Systems. Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations.

results.title: Market Information Talks for the Organic Sector 2026
results.content: Market Information Talks for the Organic Sector 2026 | Ecologic Institute. In 2024, four **Market Information Talks were held on the topics of organic grain, organic niche crops, organic meat, and value chains for communal catering**. The Ecologic Institute supports Brandenburg’s organic sector by designing, organising, and facilitating the Market Information Talks. In doing so, the Ecologic Institute contributes to strengthening organic agriculture in Brandenburg and further expanding regional value chains. Foto von Peggychoucair auf pixabay.com. On 22 October 2024, around 35 professionals gathered at Seddiner See for the market information event "Value chains for organic grain from Brandenburg". This question was at the heart of the Market Information Talk "Value Chains for Organic Meat from Brandenburg," which took place on 18 November 2024 at Gut Hesterberg near Neuruppin. This key question guided the market information event "Organic Value Chains for Community Catering," held on 19 November 2024 at Seddiner See, Germany.
